The thirteenth beta of CoSky 8.0, still for developers to try. It fixes the other seven problems the review of the whole project found: watches that hid rather than refused, streams that outlived a person's sign-in, failed writes missing from the audit log, `cosky-migrate` printing secrets, and three ways the Dashboard could sign a person out or keep the wrong sign-in. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

There is no compatibility promise before `8.0.0-rc.1`, which freezes what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists.

## Try it

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-beta.13 --dev
```

What helps most is still what we could only try on one machine: Redis Sentinel or Cluster of your own with a failover, an OIDC provider other than Keycloak, moving a 6.x installation with `cosky-migrate`, and a real network. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## Fixed

- **A watch of one Config, or of one service, that the rules leave out looked empty.** A watch was admitted whenever the subject could watch the kind at all, and what it delivered was filtered. A client watching a Config its rules do not name got an empty snapshot, and took the Config to be absent. Such a watch is now refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, as reading the Config is; a watch of the whole kind is still filtered. (#1292)
- **Streams opened by a person outlived their sign-in.** The server keeps no record of a person, and nothing ended a Watch opened with an OIDC token: it went on after the token expired, after signing out, and after the person was removed from a group at the provider. A stream now ends when its ID token expires, and the Dashboard opens it again with the renewed token. (#1292)
- **A write that failed with a timeout or a cancellation left no audit line,** though it may have landed. Every write now leaves one, with the code its caller got: `UNAVAILABLE`, `CANCELLED`, or `UNKNOWN`. (#1292)
- **`cosky-migrate` could print the token or the Redis password.** A `COSKY_TOKEN` ending in a line break, as a Kubernetes Secret made from a file gives it, failed the run with the token in the error, and a malformed source URI was printed with its password. The token is now trimmed, and neither is printed. Several sources without `--cluster` are now a usage error rather than a crash. (#1292)
- **A moment of trouble at the identity provider signed people out later.** The Dashboard dropped its refresh token on any failed renewal, a 503 during a restart included, and the person was signed out when the ID token expired. Only a refresh token the provider refuses for good is now dropped; anything else is tried again. (#1292)
- **A token pasted at the sign-in page kept an earlier OIDC sign-in.** Signing out then sent the ServiceAccount token to the provider, into its logs. Signing in with a token now ends the OIDC sign-in of the tab, and only an ID token goes to the provider. (#1292)
- **The Dashboard renewed by the provider's clock.** With the computer's clock ahead of the provider's, it renewed over and over; behind it, the server refused the token before it was renewed. Renewal now counts from when the token arrived, by the computer's own clock. (#1292)

## Upgrading from beta.12

- Nothing changes: the gRPC API, the protos, REST, the data in Redis and the properties. Applications stay on Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0. `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard come with this release.
- A client watching one Config, or one service's Instances, outside its rules now gets `PERMISSION_DENIED` instead of an empty snapshot.
- Watches opened with an OIDC token end when it expires, every 5 minutes on a default Keycloak. The Dashboard reopens them by itself; a client of your own that watches with a person's token has to do the same.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on, each replica reads every namespace every second instead. A write then takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **A late Namespace creation that takes a write before it is undone** stays, without an object, and the server logs an error. That takes a write in the round trip between making the namespace and dropping it.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.
- **The server does not stop an account from granting itself roles** it may write; see the security guide.
